newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 28.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Durable goods orders surged 2.3 percent in June.
* The beef industry won a victory as a federal judge struck down rules allowing poultry processors to sell birds without telling consumers how much water they absorb in packing.
* Bre-X shareholders sued J.P. Morgan and Lehman Brothers over the firms' ties to the Canadian company at the center of a big mining fraud.
* U.S. PC sales surged 19 percent to 21.9 percent in the second quarter.
* The future of McDonnell Douglas defense lines in St. Louis is emerging as a source of contention with Boeing.
* Ford is expected this fall to unveil a new structure and name for its $16.4 billion a year parts unit.
* General Motors averted a potential nationwide shutdown of assembly plants as the UAW approved a pact to end a six-day strike at a key transmission plant.
* Aetna promoted Richard Huber, vice president of strategy and finance, to president and chief executive.
* CellPro was found by a federal court to have willfully infringed on patents on a much-publicized cancer treatment and was ordered to pay $7 million in damages.
* NationsBank was charged with discriminatory hiring practices in a U.S. Labor Department complaint involving nearly 1,500 minority applicants.
* UPS is mounting a campaign in Congress to block the U.S. Postal Service from expanding its air-export delivery service for bulk shippers.
* America Online will collect "rent" from its electronic retailers instead of relying mainly on a cut of their sales.
* As the bond market continues to climb, mortgage bond investors are feeling increasing pressure to bail out of underperforming mortgages and get into Treasuries.

* Shares of SFX Broadcasting are climbing on speculation that the radio station operator will be the next company to be snapped up in the industry's rapid consolidation. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
